articles.title: UFC's Dana White Appears with Trump at a White House Briefing — But Won't Be His Press Secretary
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — After bringing UFC to the White House lawn this summer, President Donald Trump has now brought it to the briefing room, too.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — After bringing UFC to the White House lawn this summer , President Donald Trump has now brought it to the briefing room, too.

Trump made a surprise appearance before reporters Monday with UFC chief Dana White and briefly stood aside as his longtime friend took questions — milking a joke that began over the weekend, when Trump said he had offered White the job of White House press secretary.

"I've always wanted to do this," White said, before bellowing, "Who has the first question?" He then clarified, "I have zero political aspirations."

The joke — and the briefing — were the latest in a series of unexpected choices by the president since Republicans' sweeping losses during last week's midterm elections . Trump's briefing room stop was so hastily organized that officials didn't have time to affix the presidential seal to the lectern from which he spoke.

The president had announced on social media Saturday that he wanted "the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior" as his next chief spokesman — catching White off-guard at a boxing match in London. "He called me and told me that he had done this," White said Monday. "The last 24 hours of my life has been insane."

Trump said he had been having a "very bad press day" and thought suggesting White as the 38th White House press secretary in the nation's history might be good for a laugh.

"We thought we'd have a little fun and we brought Dana here," Trump said. "He would be fantastic."

White tells Trump, 'I do not want to be in politics, no.'

Some reporters in the press room played along. White was asked if he had any advice for Trump on the possibility of issuing a posthumous pardon for Pete Rose , baseball's all-time hits leader.

"I don't advise the president on anything ever," White responded. "But yeah, I think it's fair." Trump then interjected to say, "I'd give Pete Rose a pardon."

At one point, White marveled, "I can't believe you actually have questions for me."

Trump eventually took over. But after answering about half an hour of questions on the midterms, the war in Iran and a variety of serious topics, the president turned to White and asked, "Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America" or "just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC?"

"Thank you for the offer," White said, before allowing, "I do not want to be in politics, no."

Trump post-midterm moves have been peculiar

In the hours after Trump's Saturday post landed, neither the White House nor UFC would provide clarity on whether it was serious . Then, on Sunday night, Trump finally said, "I was kidding, but I think Dana likes the idea, and he is a very capable guy."

Trump has long relished doing the norm-busting unexpected as president, but he's leaned even more into that tendency around the election.

The day before balloting began, Trump used what was billed as a speech outlining his closing argument for why his party deserved to continue to control Congress to instead talk up his costly and problem-plagued effort to overhaul the Lincoln Memorial's Reflecting Pool.

On Wednesday, after Democrats won all over the country, including notching Senate seats in deep red states like Texas, South Carolina and Kansas, he took reporters on a tour of the White House ballroom's construction site and even signed a steel beam .

The following day, Trump declared the Oval Office would become a national monument — even though that won't prevent future presidents from undoing the gilded flourishes he's packed it with.

On Friday, the White House promoted a glitzy new website celebrating plans for a towering memorial arch in Trump's honor, despite a court order blocking work on it.

The White House press secretary position is open due to the brief, tumultuous week when Trump tried out Katie Zacharia as press secretary. She struggled in her sole appearance before reporters and left the job after five days.

The post had been vacant since Karoline Leavitt left at the end of August.

Trump has frequently attended UFC events with White. The pair have been friends for decades, and White spoke at the last three Republican National Conventions.

Trump even allowed White's sport to take over the White House's South Lawn in June for the celebration of America's 250th year of independence and the president's own 80th birthday. A wire-mesh Octagon was constructed under " The Claw ," a spaceship-like metal arch fitted with lights, sound equipment and large screens.

"He's really very unique," Trump said, describing his friend, in the White House briefing room. "The only problem is he'll talk for a little while and then he's going to beat the hell out of you."
authors: Will Weissert and Seung Min Kim, Associated Press

articles.title: Donald Trump jokes he's 'devastated' after Dana White rules out White House press secretary role
articles.summary: Following a bizarre weekend, Trump and White put the press secretary saga to rest with a joint briefing in the nation’s capital.
articles.body:
UFC CEO Dana White made his much-discussed visit to the White House on Monday, where he joined U.S. President Donald Trump for a press briefing and officially turned down the president's tongue-in-cheek offer to become his new press secretary.

Following a bizarre weekend in which Trump appeared to float the open role of White House press secretary to the UFC boss in a Truth Social post, only to admit a day later that he was "only kidding, but Dana loves the idea," Trump and White put the discussion to rest to close out a joint press briefing with the two in the nation's capital.

Trump: "So let me ask you the big question. Dana, would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America. Look at the sign — you'd have this behind all the time, 'The White House, Washington.' Would you like that or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC?" White: "Thank you for the offer, sir. I do not want to be in politics." Trump: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everyone."

Trump: "So let me ask you the big question. Dana, would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America. Look at the sign — you'd have this behind all the time, 'The White House, Washington.' Would you like that or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC?"

White: "Thank you for the offer, sir. I do not want to be in politics."

Trump: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everyone."

White briefly took questions from reporters during the press appearance, after which Trump explained how the peculiar situation first arose.

"We were having a very bad press day and I don't know why, I thought of his name," Trump said. "He's been a friend for a long time. I said, 'I think I'm going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary.' I said it to a group of the press and that was it. I was sort of kidding.

"Then they wrote the stories as though I wasn't kidding, and then [White] was inundated and I was inundated. He was here anyway and we thought we'd have a little fun and we brought Dana here. He would be fantastic."

"The last 24 hours of my life have been insane," White added.

White and Trump have maintained a close personal relationship for decades, dating back to the early days of the UFC's rise in the United States, when Trump's Atlantic City hotel and casino hosted two of the promotion's events in 2001. White has since become one of Trump's most prominent supporters in the sports world, speaking at three Republican National Conventions and publicly backing Trump's presidential campaigns.

White's initial reaction to Trump's social media post Saturday only further fueled speculation around his potential appointment. White first posted an image of himself at the podium of the White House press briefing room with the caption, "On to the next chapter," then told reporters in London that he was "flying to Washington" directly after Zuffa Boxing 12's post-fight press conference in order to meet with Trump on Monday.

Trump clarified Sunday that his meeting with White was previously scheduled and concerned unrelated matters, which both men reiterated Monday afternoon.

In the end, it appears the whole saga ended up being much ado about nothing.

articles.title: Dana White Turns Down Donald Trump’s Press Secretary Offer in Hilarious Exchange at White House
articles.summary: Dana White makes a surprise White House appearance alongside Donald Trump, turning down the President’s offer to become press secretary.
articles.body:
So, the real-life episode of The Office continues. Just two days after Donald Trump jokingly offered him the role of press secretary in his administration, Dana White made a personal appearance at the White House. For the unversed, the President had taken to his Truth Social account to announce that the UFC CEO and several other fighters were welcome to join his cabinet.

However, just a day after the announcement, Trump clarified that the offer was made in a jovial spirit and that he was only joking. While he maintained that White would be a fantastic choice for the position, he insisted that there was nothing serious behind the proposal.

The UFC CEO had confirmed that he would meet Trump on November 9 after returning to the United States from the Zuffa Boxing 12 event in London. However, the President later clarified that White's visit had nothing to do with the press secretary offer. According to Trump, the UFC boss was already planning to be in Washington and had simply decided to stop by and see him.

And that is exactly what White ended up doing. During the November 9 White House news conference alongside Trump, White officially turned down the prospect of becoming press secretary.

While admitting that he doesn't say no to the President, the UFC CEO made it clear that he had no interest in entering politics at the moment. He said, "I don't tell the president no to anything. I didn't say no. Literally every media outlet was calling me, and I didn't want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first."

Trump then added to the bizarre nature of the situation by reiterating that he had been joking about the entire proposition. He said, "We were having a very bad press day, and I don't know why, I thought of his name; he's been a friend for a long time. I said I think I'm going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary. I said it to a group of the press, and that was it. I was sort of kidding."

The President further explained, "Then they wrote the stories as though I wasn't kidding, and then [Dana] was inundated and I was inundated. He was here anyway, and we thought we'd have a little fun and we brought Dana here. He would be fantastic."

White's rejection then became the subject of another lighthearted exchange when Trump jokingly asked him whether he would leave " the ridiculous UFC " to accept the position in his administration. White responded, "Thank you for the offer, sir. I do not want to be in politics."

Keeping the laughter-filled atmosphere going, Trump claimed he was "devastated" by White's response before bringing the briefing to a close.
